title: Zero Credentials. 1,500 Packages Exposed.
caption:
I let my coding agent pick dependencies, and I have never once checked who publishes them.

Bloom Security found npm's Trusted Publishing was binding each package to a GitHub repo name, not the permanent numeric ID GitHub puts in the very same token. Rename or delete that repo and the name frees up. Claim it, add a workflow file with the matching name, trigger it, and npm hands you a publish token for a package you don't own. No stolen credential. No compromised account. 1,500+ packages with 10M+ downloads were exposed.

Nobody knows whether it was ever used in the wild. What gets me is the attestation: a release published this way is still signed, just against the attacker's repo, so anything that only asks "is it signed" waves it through.

Reported June 6. Last reply July 8. Six follow-ups, no answer. The fix landed October 2, and Bloom only found out by re-running its own test. PyPI has checked the numeric ID since launch. Do you audit your deps?

Zero Credentials.
1,500 Packages Exposed.
slides.sub: npm's Trusted Publishing bound each package to a GitHub repo name. Claim the abandoned name, get a publish token.

slides.headline: 70 Packages A Month
slides.sub: Bloom's telemetry across dozens of orgs: about 70 agent installs a month per endpoint, close to 350 on developer machines.

slides.title: The Name, Not The ID
slides.sub: GitHub's token carries repository_id, a number that survives renames. npm stored only the owner/repo slug and never checked it.

slides.title: Four Steps, No Theft
items: Claim the freed owner/repo slug on GitHub
Add a workflow file with the bound filename
Trigger it. GitHub mints an OIDC token
Exchange it at npm for a publish credential

slides.title: Signed By The Attacker
slides.sub: The release carries a valid provenance attestation signed against the attacker's repo. Tooling that only asks "is it signed" passes it.

slides.title: Six Follow-Ups, No Reply
slides.sub: Reported June 6, validated June 9, last reply July 8. Fix shipped October 2. Bloom found out by retesting.

slides.title: Run npm trust list
items: Check each binding still points at a repo you own
Renamed or transferred? Re-create the binding
Publish once right after creating a binding
Delete the binding before the repo
